status.en: 5 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 55% fewer than the week before, most of them in Kivu, Kigali and Kinshasa.
status.nb: 5 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 55 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Kivu, Kigali og Kinshasa.

summary.en: IS-linked militants attacked an Ebola clinic in eastern DR Congo, forcing patients to flee and killing dozens of civilians, while ADF fighters assaulted villages in North Kivu, killing 33 residents. The United Nations peacekeeping mission is set to leave the country in December, and the United States has sanctioned Rwanda’s defence ministry and its military bank Zigama. Joseph Kabila now heads a rebel coalition that includes M23, which has taken positions in Rugezi after a week of fighting with government troops. 1,158 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: IS-tilknyttede militante angrep på en ebolaklinikk i østlige DR Kongo, tvang pasienter til å flykte og drepte dusinvis av sivile, mens ADF-krigere angrep landsbyer i Nord-Kivu og drepte 33 innbyggere. FN-fredsbevaringsmisjonen skal forlate landet i desember, og USA har sanksjonert Rwandas forsvarsdepartement og den militære banken Zigama. Joseph Kabila leder nå en opprørskoalisjon som inkluderer M23‑opprørerne, som har tatt posisjoner i Rugezi etter en ukes kamper med regjeringsstyrker. 1 158 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: M23 campaign (2022–present)
background.extract: The M23 campaign is an ongoing series of military offensives launched by the March 23 Movement (M23), a Rwandan-backed rebel paramilitary group in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, since March 2022. In November 2021, M23 first launched attacks against the Congolese military (FARDC) and MONUSCO, seizing military positions in Ndiza, Cyanzu, and Runyoni in North Kivu Province. This coincided with the deployment of Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) to the region to combat the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a Ugandan rebel group operating in the Congo's North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
